description.narrative: The project aims to provide efficient transportation on the Greater Mekong Subregion (GMS) Southern Economic Corridor (SEC), which passes through Cambodia, through the improvement of the national road sections in Prey Veng, Siem Reap, and Svay Rieng provinces of Cambodia that are unsafe and prone to flooding. The project will also (i) support the Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MPWT) in road asset management by (a) strengthening its axle load control operation, (b) introducing a quality assurance system, and (c) improving road maintenance execution; and (ii) help project communities in improving their safety and health by implementing a gender-responsive community-based road safety program and an HIV/AIDS and human trafficking awareness and prevention program (HTAP).

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Axle load control enhanced Indicator: At least six weigh stations refurbished (2016 baseline: 0) Achievement: 6 Progress/Status: Civil works completed by 31 December 2020. Data Source: Project progress report

Output: Axle load control enhanced Indicator: At least two weigh scales and vehicles for two mobile teams provided (2016 baseline: 0) Achievement: 2 Progress/Status: Completed. Contracts were awarded and equipment delivered. Data Source: Project progress report

Output: More safe and climate-resilient national roads delivered Indicator: 104 km of NR6 received periodic maintenance (2016 baseline: 0) Achievement: 93.23 Progress/Status: The rehabilitation and improvement works under the CW-3 NR6 contract was completed in June 2020. Maintenance works commenced immediately. As of 30 June 2023, maintenance works for CW-3 and CW-A2 were 100% complete. Data Source: Construction completion report

Output: More safe and climate-resilient national roads delivered Indicator: 97 km of NR1 rehabilitated (2016 baseline: 0) Achievement: 95.70 Progress/Status: Rehabilitation and improvement works under the CW-1 NR1 and CW-2 NR1 contracts were completed in October 2020. Maintenance works commenced immediately. As of 30 June 2023, maintenance works for CW-1 and CW-2 were 100% complete. Data Source: Construction completion report

Output: More safe and climate-resilient national roads delivered Indicator: At least 20% of unskilled labor days under the civil works contracts undertaken by women (2016 baseline: 0) Achievement: 27.45 Progress/Status: Rehabilitation and improvement works under the CW-1 NR1 and CW-2 NR1 contracts were completed in October 2020 and for CW-3 NR6 in June 2020. Maintenance works under these 3 contracts commenced right after and were completed by 30 June 2023.
As of June 2023, the cumulative number of women hired for unskilled labor is 27.45% or 57,280 labor days out of 208,700 unskilled laborers hired. This is over the target of 20%.
Data Source: Project benefit monitoring report

Output: More safe and climate-resilient national roads delivered Indicator: At least 24 km of NR1 and NR6 improved with various climate resilience features (2016 baseline 0) Achievement: 23.89 Progress/Status: Completed. As of 30 November 2022, 23.889 km of NR1 and NR6 improved. Data Source: Construction completion report

Output: More safe and climate-resilient national roads delivered Indicator: At least 3.4 km of guardrails and 700 guide posts installed on the project roads (2016 baseline: 0) Achievement: .685 Progress/Status: 685 meters of guardrails only and 2,110 guide posts were installed. Data Source: Construction completion report

Output: More safe and climate-resilient national roads delivered Indicator: Rehabilitate 8 lanes of roads of NR6 (2016 baseline: 0) Achievement: 8 Progress/Status: 5.8km of NR6 in Siem Reap downtown rehabilitated comprising 8 lanes road Data Source: Project progress report

Output: Quality assurance for civil works in the Ministry of Public Works and Transport strengthened Indicator: More than 50% of material quality control testing performed on government-funded roads (2016 baseline: Not applicable) Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: As of 30 November 2022, achieved 100% of material quality control testing performed on government funded roads with the estimated budget about 1% of the total civil work budget. Data Source: Project progress report

Output: Quality assurance for civil works in the Ministry of Public Works and Transport strengthened Indicator: Quality assurance audit annually conducted on 20% of ongoing road works of MPWT starting in 2020. (2016 baseline: 0 audits conducted) Achievement: 20 Progress/Status: As per the EA's advice on 22 December 2023, quality assurance audit were performed on 20% of government-funded roads. Data Source: Project progress report

Output: Road safety enforcement in project communes improved Indicator: At least 10 safe school zones established (2016 baseline: 0) Achievement: 66 Progress/Status: Completed under the CW-1 NR1, CW-2 NR1 and CW-3 NR6 contracts. A total of 66 safe school zones were established along project roads. Data Source: Project progress report

Output: Road safety enforcement in project communes improved Indicator: At least 50,000 residents with increased awareness of traffic safety, of which are 30% are women (2016 baseline: 0) Achievement: 7716 Progress/Status: As of 30 June 2023, a total of 52,384 community members participated in the road safety awareness activities. This was over the target of 50,000. Women participants comprised 29,062 which is 55% of the total number of participants and was over the target of 30% women only.
A total of 66 safe school zones were established along project roads under the contracts CW-1 NR1, CW-2 NR1, CW-3 NR6 and CW-A2 NR6. Data Source: Project progress report
Transport efficiency increased on the national road sections along Greater Mekong Subregion Southern Economic Corridor.

Average daily vehicle-km increased to 2.252 million for NR1 and 0.995 million for NR6 (2016 baseline: 1.422 million for NR1 and 0.633 million for NR6) Achievement: 31.7 Progress/Status: As of 30 June 2023, overall project progress is 100% with time elapsed of 100% (63 months out of 63 months).
The PICS contract was signed in October 2018 and mobilization was in November 2018. Activities were completed by 30 June 2023.
Output 1: All civil works were completed by April 2022. Maintenance works for CW-1 NR1, CW-2 NR, CW-3 NR6 and CW-A2 NR6 were 100% complete as of 30 June 2023. As of June 2023, the cumulative number of women hired for unskilled labor was 27.45% or 57,280 labor days out of 208,700 unskilled laborers hired. This was over the target of 20%. The targets under this output were partially achieved because only 685 meters of guardrails out of the 3.4 kms target were installed.
Output 2: All activities under this output were achieved.
Output 3: As per the EA's advice during the loan review mission's (4-9 June 2023) wrap-up meeting on 14 July 2023, 3 out of 4 laboratories were handed over. Training on the use of the laboratory equipment was completed. For the other activity: quality assurance audit annually conducted on 20% of ongoing road works, MPWT advised during the review mission that the quality assurance audit will be conducted after the loan closing date due to the delayed installation of the laboratory equipment and handing over of laboratories. The quality assurance audit will commence after the laboratories and equipment have been handed-over to the MPWT Central Laboratory. Targets under this output were only partially achieved as of 30 June 2023, the loan closing date.
Output 4: As of 30 June 2023, a total of 52,384 community members participated in the road safety awareness activities. This was over the target of 50,000. Women participants comprised 29,062 which is 55% of the total number of participants. Target was only 30% women. A total of 66 safe school zones were established along project roads under the contracts CW-1 NR1, CW-2 NR1, CW-3 NR6 and CW-A2 NR6. All targets under this output were achieved. Data Source: Project benefit monitoring report Baseline value: TBD
